summary: The main article describes a visible-light-mediated three-component dicarbofunctionalization of styrenes using benzylic pyridinium salts as radical precursors. It includes one optimization table, three schemes detailing the scope and mechanism, and a TOC graphic summarizing the transformation.

items.heading: Scheme 1. Activated amines as radical precursors and dicarbofunctionalization of olefins.
items.description: This scheme contrasts the use of carboxylic acids versus amines as radical precursors and outlines the general strategy for undirected intermolecular three-component dicarbofunctionalization.

items.heading: Table 1. Three-component dicarbofunctionalization using benzylic radicals.
items.description: Optimization table comparing different benzylic radical precursors (bromides vs. pyridinium salts), photocatalysts, and additives for the dicarbofunctionalization reaction.

items.heading: Scheme 2. Scope of the visible-light-mediated deaminative dicarbofunctionalization.
items.description: Comprehensive scope showing the variation of benzylic Katritzky salts, styrenes, and nucleophilic arenes (indoles and anilines) to produce diverse 1,1-diarylalkanes.

items.heading: Scheme 3. Applications of the deaminative dicarbofunctionalization of styrenes and radical clock experiment.
items.description: Demonstrates the application of the method to dipeptides, a spirocyclization reaction, and a radical clock experiment to support the proposed mechanism.

items.heading: Scheme 4. Proposed mechanism of the deaminative dicarbofunctionalization using Katritzky salts as radical precursors.
items.description: A detailed catalytic cycle showing the reduction of the Katritzky salt, radical addition to styrene, and subsequent trapping of the resulting cation by a nucleophile.

items.heading: TOC graphic
items.description: Table of Contents graphic summarizing the three-component coupling of benzylic pyridinium salts, styrenes, and indoles under visible light.
